title: Pancreatic Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - the physician decides. ONCOTREE navigator for pancreatic adenocarcinoma: workup -> resectability / stage stratification -> stage-specific arms (resectable / borderline / locally advanced / metastatic). Every arm is REFINED before a recommendation: resectable and borderline route neoadjuvant -> response-adapted restaging -> resection -> adjuvant by fitness -> surveillance; locally advanced routes induction -> restage -> consolidation or conversion; metastatic routes biomarker (germline BRCA/PALB2, MSI/MMR) then line-of-therapy (first line -> response -> second line -> later line), with platinum-enabled olaparib maintenance. Surveillance feeds a recurrence pathway into the metastatic line-of-therapy sub-tree. Treatment leaves route to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference only; regimens without a dose protocol (gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel, gemcitabine monotherapy, chemoradiation / SBRT, best supportive care, gemcitabine + capecitabine) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Invents no dose or regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses. FollowCare-style safety: never changes prescriptions, does not diagnose definitively, does not stop medications.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma, and general references (DeVita, Harrison). Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers; no proprietary guideline text reproduced.

a.text: Resectability is defined by tumor relationship to the celiac axis, common hepatic artery, superior mesenteric artery and vein / portal vein on high-quality pancreatic-protocol CT; classify at a multidisciplinary tumor board.

b.text: mFOLFIRINOX is preferred for fit patients (good performance status, adequate organ function, bilirubin controlled); gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel is the main alternative when a triplet is not tolerable.

c.text: Offer germline testing to every patient with confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and somatic tumor profiling in metastatic disease (BRCA1/2, PALB2, MSI/MMR, NTRK, KRAS, HER2).

d.text: Olaparib maintenance applies to a germline BRCA1/2 mutation with disease control after at least about 4 months of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy; it is not indicated after progression on platinum.

e.text: Restage after neoadjuvant / induction therapy at about 2-4 months with pancreatic-protocol CT and CA 19-9; proceed to resection only if there is no progression and a margin-negative resection appears technically feasible.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and staging assessment
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation before treatment. Confirm adenocarcinoma, assess extent of disease and biliary status, and send germline testing.
bullets: History, physical, performance status: weight loss, jaundice, pain, new-onset diabetes, family cancer history
Pancreatic-protocol multiphase CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (or MRI); defines resectability and metastatic disease
Tissue confirmation of adenocarcinoma (EUS-guided FNA/biopsy preferred; biopsy a metastatic site if present)
Baseline CA 19-9 after biliary decompression; endoscopic stent before chemotherapy if bilirubin elevated
Germline testing for all patients (BRCA1/2, PALB2, MMR) and somatic profiling in metastatic disease; nutrition, enzyme replacement, pain assessment

nodes.name: Stage / resectability
nodes.title: Stage and resectability at presentation
nodes.description: Classify the disease. Resectability of non-metastatic disease is decided by tumor-vessel contact on imaging at a multidisciplinary board.
bullets: Resectable: no arterial contact; no or minimal (<=180 degrees) venous contact without vein distortion
Borderline resectable: limited artery contact or reconstructable vein involvement (>180 degrees or short-segment occlusion)
Locally advanced: unresectable by vessel encasement, no distant metastases
Metastatic: distant spread (liver, peritoneum, lung, distant nodes)

tables.title: Resectability by tumor-vessel relationship (simplified)
rows: No contact, or <=180 degrees without distortion
Contact <=180 degrees, or CHA short-segment contact

nodes.name: Resectable: approach
nodes.title: Resectable disease: upfront surgery vs neoadjuvant
nodes.description: Choose surgery-first or neoadjuvant therapy. Favor neoadjuvant when high-risk features are present (markedly elevated CA 19-9, large primary, bulky nodes, borderline imaging).
bullets: Upfront resection is acceptable for clearly resectable disease without high-risk features
Neoadjuvant therapy is increasingly preferred to treat micrometastases early and select biology
Any approach: complete perioperative chemotherapy totalling about 6 months when tolerated

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant regimen
nodes.title: Resectable: neoadjuvant regimen by fitness
nodes.description: Select neoadjuvant chemotherapy by fitness, then restage and proceed to resection if still resectable.
bullets: Fit patients: modified FOLFIRINOX (triplet)
Reduced fitness: gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel
Plan restaging with CT and CA 19-9 at about 2-4 months

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX
nodes.title: Neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX
nodes.description: Preferred neoadjuvant option in fit patients; then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: Modified FOLFIRINOX for about 2-4 months (dose engine computes patient doses)
Monitor neutropenia, neuropathy, diarrhea; growth-factor support as needed
Then restage before resection (next step)

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant gem + nab-paclitaxel
nodes.title: Neoadjuvant gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel
nodes.description: Alternative neoadjuvant option when a triplet is not suitable; then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: Gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel; monitor cytopenias and neuropathy
Then restage before resection (next step)

nodes.name: Restage after neoadjuvant
nodes.title: Resectable: response-adapted restaging
nodes.description: Restage after neoadjuvant therapy. Proceed to resection only if there is no progression and a margin-negative resection is feasible.
bullets: No progression + resectable: proceed to surgery
Local progression without metastases: manage as locally advanced
New distant metastases: move to the metastatic pathway

nodes.name: Resection
nodes.title: Pancreatic resection (Whipple / distal / total)
nodes.description: Margin-negative resection with regional lymphadenectomy, then adjuvant chemotherapy.
bullets: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (head/uncinate), distal pancreatectomy + splenectomy (body/tail), or total pancreatectomy as anatomy dictates
Regional lymphadenectomy; document margin (R0 vs R1) and node status
Then adjuvant chemotherapy by fitness (next step)

nodes.name: Adjuvant regimen
nodes.title: After resection: choose adjuvant regimen
nodes.description: Resection complete with recovery. Select adjuvant chemotherapy by fitness; aim to start within about 12 weeks, total perioperative chemotherapy about 6 months.
bullets: Confirm adequate recovery, performance status, and organ function
Deduct neoadjuvant months already given from the total 6-month target
Discuss postoperative chemoradiation only in selected margin-positive / node-positive cases

nodes.name: Adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX
nodes.title: Adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX (fit patients)
nodes.description: Preferred adjuvant regimen after resection in fit patients; strongest survival benefit.
bullets: Modified FOLFIRINOX to complete about 6 months total perioperative therapy
Monitor neutropenia, neuropathy, diarrhea; growth-factor support as needed
Then surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Adjuvant gemcitabine-based
nodes.title: Adjuvant gemcitabine-based (reduced fitness)
nodes.description: For patients not fit for a triplet.
bullets: Gemcitabine + capecitabine, or gemcitabine monotherapy, for about 6 months
Monitor counts and hepatic / renal function; then surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Borderline: strategy
nodes.title: Borderline resectable: neoadjuvant strategy
nodes.description: Neoadjuvant therapy is standard for borderline disease to improve margin-negative resection. Do not go directly to surgery.
bullets: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is preferred; restage after about 2-4 months
Add chemoradiation / SBRT when the vessel margin is the main concern
Resect only if downstaged / stable and technically feasible

nodes.name: Borderline neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX
nodes.title: Borderline: neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX
nodes.description: Preferred neoadjuvant chemotherapy for fit borderline patients; then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: Modified FOLFIRINOX; gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel if a triplet is not tolerable
Monitor neutropenia, neuropathy, diarrhea
Then restage before resection (next step)

nodes.name: Borderline chemo then RT
nodes.title: Borderline: induction chemotherapy then chemoradiation / SBRT
nodes.description: Induction chemotherapy followed by radiation, especially where the vessel margin is the concern; then restaging.
bullets: Induction mFOLFIRINOX (or gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel), then chemoradiation or SBRT
Radiation regimen has no dose protocol here - shown as guidance (radiation oncology plans)
Then restage before resection (next step)

nodes.name: Borderline restage
nodes.title: Borderline: response-adapted restaging
nodes.description: Restage after neoadjuvant / induction therapy. Resect only if a margin-negative resection is feasible.
bullets: Downstaged / stable and resectable: proceed to surgery, then adjuvant chemotherapy
Stable but still unresectable locally: manage as locally advanced
New distant metastases: move to the metastatic pathway

nodes.name: Borderline resection
nodes.title: Borderline: margin-negative resection after downstaging
nodes.description: Resection with venous / arterial reconstruction as needed, then adjuvant chemotherapy.
bullets: Resection with vein resection / reconstruction as required for margin clearance
Document margin (R0 vs R1) and node status
Then adjuvant chemotherapy by fitness (next step)

nodes.name: Locally advanced
nodes.title: Locally advanced (unresectable, M0): induction by fitness
nodes.description: Systemic therapy is the backbone; consolidative radiation is selective. Choose induction by performance status.
bullets: Induction systemic chemotherapy for about 4-6 months, then reassess
Consider consolidative chemoradiation / SBRT if no distant progression
A minority convert to resectable - re-evaluate at a tumor board

nodes.name: LA induction mFOLFIRINOX
nodes.title: Locally advanced: induction mFOLFIRINOX
nodes.description: Preferred induction chemotherapy in fit locally advanced patients; then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: Modified FOLFIRINOX induction; gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel is an alternative
Monitor neutropenia, neuropathy, diarrhea
Then restage to decide consolidation vs conversion (next step)

nodes.name: LA gemcitabine / supportive
nodes.title: Locally advanced: gemcitabine-based or supportive care (poor PS)
nodes.description: For patients with poor performance status.
bullets: Gemcitabine monotherapy (or gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel if tolerable)
If not a chemotherapy candidate, move to best supportive care (next step)
nodes.linkLabel: Best supportive care if not a chemotherapy candidate

nodes.name: LA restage
nodes.title: Locally advanced: response-adapted restaging
nodes.description: Restage after induction. A good response may permit conversion surgery; otherwise consolidate or treat as metastatic.
bullets: Converted to resectable: proceed to surgery, then adjuvant chemotherapy
Stable / no distant progression: consolidative chemoradiation or SBRT
New distant metastases: move to the metastatic pathway

nodes.name: LA consolidation RT
nodes.title: Locally advanced: consolidative chemoradiation / SBRT
nodes.description: Consolidative radiation after stable disease on induction chemotherapy.
bullets: Chemoradiation or SBRT after induction, if no distant progression
Radiation regimen has no dose protocol here - shown as guidance (radiation oncology plans)
Then surveillance; treat distant relapse on the metastatic pathway

nodes.name: Best supportive care
nodes.title: Best supportive / palliative care
nodes.description: Symptom-directed care when disease-directed therapy is not appropriate or desired.
bullets: Prioritize pain control, biliary and GI patency, nutrition, and pancreatic enzyme replacement
Manage thromboembolism risk, depression, and glycemic control
Early palliative-care involvement and hospice referral as appropriate

nodes.name: Metastatic biomarker
nodes.title: Metastatic: biomarker direction
nodes.description: Check germline and somatic profiling first. An actionable biomarker changes the pathway; otherwise choose first-line by fitness.
bullets: Confirm germline BRCA1/2 and PALB2, and tumor MSI/MMR, NTRK, KRAS, HER2
MSI-H / dMMR: immunotherapy is an option in any line
Germline BRCA/PALB2: use a platinum-based first line to enable maintenance

tables.title: Actionable biomarkers in metastatic pancreatic cancer
rows: Platinum first line, then olaparib maintenance

nodes.name: MSI-H immunotherapy
nodes.title: MSI-H / dMMR: pembrolizumab
nodes.description: Microsatellite-instability-high or mismatch-repair-deficient metastatic disease.
bullets: Pembrolizumab under the tissue-agnostic MSI-H / dMMR indication (any line)
Confirm MSI/MMR status on tumor tissue; monitor for immune-related toxicity
On progression, use fitness-directed cytotoxic chemotherapy (next step)

nodes.name: BRCA: platinum fitness
nodes.title: Germline BRCA/PALB2: fitness for platinum
nodes.description: Use a platinum-containing first line so that olaparib maintenance becomes available on disease control.
bullets: Platinum-based chemotherapy is preferred (FOLFIRINOX contains oxaliplatin)
Continue platinum first line for at least about 4 months before maintenance
Gemcitabine + cisplatin is an alternative platinum backbone

nodes.name: BRCA platinum FOLFIRINOX
nodes.title: BRCA/PALB2: first-line FOLFIRINOX (platinum)
nodes.description: Platinum-based first line for germline BRCA/PALB2 metastatic disease; then a maintenance decision.
bullets: FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin-containing) as the platinum backbone
Continue at least about 4 months; monitor neuropathy and cumulative oxaliplatin
Then a maintenance decision on disease control (next step)

nodes.name: BRCA gemcitabine-based
nodes.title: BRCA/PALB2, reduced fitness: gemcitabine + cisplatin
nodes.description: When platinum FOLFIRINOX is not tolerable; retain a platinum for BRCA sensitivity where feasible.
bullets: Gemcitabine + cisplatin (platinum retained), or gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel if platinum not tolerated
Olaparib maintenance requires a platinum first line - not applicable without it
On progression, proceed to second-line therapy (next step)

nodes.name: BRCA maintenance decision
nodes.title: BRCA/PALB2: maintenance decision after platinum
nodes.description: After about 4+ months of platinum with disease control, transition to maintenance olaparib; if progressing on platinum, olaparib is not indicated.
bullets: Disease controlled after >= 4 months platinum: switch to maintenance olaparib
Progression on platinum: move to second-line chemotherapy
Continue supportive care and monitor counts

nodes.name: Maintenance olaparib
nodes.title: BRCA maintenance: olaparib
nodes.description: Maintenance PARP inhibitor after disease control on platinum-based first line in germline BRCA1/2 disease.
bullets: Start olaparib after at least about 4 months of platinum first-line with disease control
Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity; monitor counts (myelosuppression)
On progression, resume cytotoxic chemotherapy (second-line pathway)

nodes.name: Metastatic first line
nodes.title: Metastatic first line (no actionable biomarker)
nodes.description: Choose first-line chemotherapy by performance status and organ function.
bullets: Good PS: FOLFIRINOX preferred; moderate PS: gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel
Poor PS: gemcitabine monotherapy or best supportive care
Reassess response and tolerance at intervals; plan for second line

nodes.name: First-line FOLFIRINOX
nodes.title: Metastatic first line: FOLFIRINOX
nodes.description: Preferred first line for fit metastatic patients; then response-adapted next step.
bullets: FOLFIRINOX; monitor neutropenia, diarrhea, neuropathy
Continue supportive care, nutrition, and pain control
Then reassess response to plan maintenance vs second line (next step)

nodes.name: First-line gem + nab-paclitaxel
nodes.title: Metastatic first line: gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel
nodes.description: Standard first line for patients with moderate performance status; then response-adapted next step.
bullets: Gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel; monitor cytopenias and neuropathy
Then reassess response to plan maintenance vs second line (next step)

nodes.name: First-line gem / supportive
nodes.title: Metastatic first line: gemcitabine mono or supportive care
nodes.description: For patients with poor performance status.
bullets: Gemcitabine monotherapy for borderline-fit patients
Prioritize symptom control, biliary/GI patency, nutrition, and pain
If not a chemotherapy candidate, move to best supportive care (next step)

nodes.name: First-line response
nodes.title: Metastatic: first-line response assessment
nodes.description: Reassess after first-line therapy. Ongoing response may allow a maintenance / de-escalation approach; progression triggers a non-cross-resistant second line.
bullets: Ongoing response / stable and tolerating: consider maintenance or de-escalation
Progression: switch to a non-cross-resistant second line
Re-check performance status and organ function before continuing

nodes.name: Maintenance / de-escalation
nodes.title: Metastatic: maintenance / de-escalation on response
nodes.description: Continuation or de-escalation of an active regimen for responders without an actionable target.
bullets: Continue an active, tolerated regimen, or de-escalate (e.g. drop oxaliplatin for cumulative neuropathy, continue fluoropyrimidine)
No dedicated maintenance dose protocol here - shown as guidance
Reassess at intervals; move to the next line on progression

nodes.name: Metastatic second line
nodes.title: Metastatic second line (by prior regimen)
nodes.description: Select a non-cross-resistant second line after first-line progression, based on what was already given.
bullets: After gemcitabine-based first line: switch to a fluoropyrimidine + irinotecan regimen
After FOLFIRINOX first line: switch to a gemcitabine-based regimen
Re-check performance status and organ function before second line

nodes.name: Second-line FOLFIRI / nal-IRI
nodes.title: Second line after gemcitabine: fluoropyrimidine + irinotecan
nodes.description: Non-cross-resistant second line after a gemcitabine-based first line; then response-adapted next step.
bullets: Liposomal irinotecan + 5-FU/leucovorin (nal-IRI); FOLFIRI is a practical alternative
Monitor diarrhea and neutropenia; irinotecan dose per UGT1A1 where relevant
Then reassess response (next step)

nodes.name: Second-line gemcitabine-based
nodes.title: Second line after FOLFIRINOX: gemcitabine-based
nodes.description: Switch to a gemcitabine-based regimen after FOLFIRINOX progression; then response-adapted next step.
bullets: Gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine monotherapy if less fit
Then reassess response (next step)

nodes.name: Second-line response
nodes.title: Metastatic: second-line response assessment
nodes.description: Reassess after second-line therapy. Continued benefit supports maintenance; progression moves to later-line options and clinical trials.
bullets: Ongoing benefit / stable: continue or de-escalate (maintenance)
Progression: later-line therapy, clinical trial, or best supportive care
Re-check performance status; many patients transition to supportive care

nodes.name: Later-line / trial / BSC
nodes.title: Metastatic later line: clinical trial or best supportive care
nodes.description: Later-line options after progression through two lines.
bullets: Clinical trial is preferred where available; re-review somatic profiling for a rare actionable target (NTRK, KRAS G12C, HER2)
A third cytotoxic line only for maintained performance status and organ function
Otherwise best supportive care / hospice; no dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Monitoring after curative-intent therapy; enter the recurrence pathway if disease returns.
bullets: History, physical, and CA 19-9 every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis every 3-6 months for 2 years, then as indicated
Address exocrine insufficiency, diabetes, nutrition, and psychosocial needs
A rising CA 19-9 or new lesion prompts restaging

nodes.name: Continue surveillance
nodes.title: No recurrence: continue surveillance
nodes.description: Maintain the monitoring schedule and survivorship care.
bullets: Continue CA 19-9 and imaging cadence as above
Ongoing pancreatic enzyme replacement, glycemic control, and nutrition
Re-image promptly for new symptoms or a rising CA 19-9

nodes.name: Recurrence type
nodes.title: Recurrence: isolated local vs distant
nodes.description: Distinguish an isolated local / regional recurrence from distant metastatic relapse; re-biopsy and re-profile where feasible.
bullets: Restage with CT (or PET-CT) and CA 19-9; biopsy to confirm and re-profile if not previously done
Isolated local / regional relapse: chemotherapy +/- local therapy, occasionally re-resection
Distant relapse: manage on the metastatic line-of-therapy pathway

nodes.name: Local recurrence
nodes.title: Isolated local / regional recurrence
nodes.description: Systemic therapy is the backbone; local therapy is selective.
bullets: Systemic chemotherapy directed by prior therapy and disease-free interval (see the metastatic line-of-therapy options)
Consider chemoradiation / SBRT if not previously irradiated and disease is isolated
Re-resection only rarely, at a multidisciplinary board for a late isolated relapse
